data.narrative:
Q-Factor is a seed-stage quantum computing company that has raised $24M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 11 peers—3 public companies (IonQ, Rigetti Computing, D-Wave Quantum) and 8 private firms including Quantinuum and Infleqtion—though the private peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables for robust median-based pricing.

The stage-progression method is the applicable triangulation approach here. Using total raised ($24M) as a base proxy and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier from seed to next-stage yields an implied valuation of $60M. This method accounts for the typical value creation and capital requirements expected between rounds at this stage.

The Peer-Median method was not applicable. While six quantum computing peers exist in the broader dataset, none met narrow-stage filters (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation tier), falling short of the three-comparable minimum for statistical reliability. Broadening to all-sector medians would risk material distortion given stage and maturity variance within quantum computing.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $51M (low) to $69M (high), with a median of $60M. Primary uncertainties include the absence of tight peer stage-comparables and the broader nascency of private quantum computing valuations. The derived range reflects stage-typical progression multiples rather than market-traded comparables.
